parts: Big-Foot de Thalek

Our story as breeders began quite a few years ago, when my husband decided he wanted the dog of his dreams: an Old English Sheepdog. He had always wanted one and, of course, with my love of animals, I did not take much convincing. That was how we came to find our first dog, Bobby. He was not a show dog, but he was the champion of our hearts, giving us everything and asking for nothing in return. He had such a gentle, sweet nature. Thanks to him, we fell completely in love with the breed.

Later, after visiting several dog shows, we decided we wanted an Old English Sheepdog like the ones we had seen there. Our search led us to our girl Wanda (Bosca). She was the most stunning puppy in her litter. We raised Bosca and Bobby together, and kept going to shows to watch and learn, although we were not yet showing our own dogs.

We decided to bring home another female to help lay the foundations of our kennel. That was when Thalek came into our lives. She was a wonderful girl, but sadly she passed away at just four months old. I fell into a deep depression, and it was Bosca and Bobby who helped me through it.

At the Medina de Pomar dog show, we were lucky enough to meet José Luis Bravo, who was then President of the Old English Sheepdog Club of Spain. We asked what he thought of Bosca, and he told us he liked her very much. He encouraged us to show her, but we were still unsure. We met him again in Santander, where we spent the whole day watching him prepare his dog and learning more about the breed. He invited us to his home and to the first Guadarrama dog show. That was when our real journey in the show ring began. José Luis taught me how to groom, brush and show Old English Sheepdogs, giving me the foundation of knowledge I have continued to build on over the years.

We decided to register a kennel name, and of course I could never forget my girl Thalek. With their full coats, Old English Sheepdogs have such enormous-looking feet that we thought of the name "Big-Foot".
And that was how we were granted the kennel name "Big-Foot de Thalek", registration number 8.852.

As the years went by, we decided to welcome a Shih Tzu: a breed with a temperament and beauty similar to the Old English Sheepdog, but in a smaller package that could share the sofa without pushing us off... We wanted a female from a well-established bloodline. We searched among breeders throughout Spain until we found our girl Amistad Sincera (Miss).

We also loved Persian cats, so we decided to bring home a female. Once our magnificent stud cat joined us, we began breeding these wonderful cats. We applied for the same name we used for our dog kennel.
We are still writing the rest of our story...

Our little family lives surrounded by nature. Our breeding philosophy is to have only a few, occasional litters, always respecting our girls' wellbeing, out of love for the animals who are part of our family. We always strive for the highest quality, carefully choosing breeding pairs that complement one another. We select our breeding dogs for their health, temperament and adherence to the breed standard, and show them to have our work independently assessed.
Caring for our family is a round-the-clock commitment.

All our animals enjoy a normal family life, sharing our everyday routines, going on daily walks and enjoying the sunshine, snow, rain and swims in the river... And we cherish our time with them, because they give us what matters most: their companionship and affection.

We spare no expense in giving them the best possible care. We feed them high-quality food, with each animal receiving the variety that suits their needs, and use the best care products and supplements. They are looked after by a vet who knows them individually and sees them regularly. They receive annual vaccinations and are treated for internal and external parasites several times a year.

Our care for each litter begins at mating, and we are personally present for every birth. From the moment each puppy is born, we monitor their weight, condition, feeding, stools and development... We spend sleepless nights watching over them during those first precious days. We get to know each puppy's personality and give them plenty of gentle handling, cuddles and affection. They receive positive early experiences and thorough socialisation, meeting children, adults, cats and the other animals in our family. We introduce all of this gradually, as the puppies grow and are ready for each new stage. Our little ones do not leave us until they are truly ready, fully weaned and independent of their mother, usually at almost four months old. We try to stay in touch with all our puppies, especially during the first few months, to see how they are developing and settling into their new homes. We build relationships with their new owners, offering our friendship, knowledge and support, and advice on giving their little one the best possible care.

We stand behind our dogs' temperaments. Alongside striving to breed the finest dogs, as close as possible to the breed standard, our guiding principle is to raise dogs with wonderful temperaments: the sweet, affectionate natures these breeds are known for.
We also offer grooming and show handling services.
For more information, please get in touch by phone, email or WhatsApp.
Breeding is not about producing puppies; it is about caring for a breed.
WHAT DOES IT MEAN TO BE A BREEDER?
A Breeder (with a capital B) is someone with a thirst for knowledge, who never truly knows it all. Someone who constantly weighs decisions of conscience, practicality and commitment.
A Breeder sacrifices personal interests, time, friendships, fine furniture and carpets for the sake of their beloved dogs.
They set aside dreams of a luxury cruise and make a major dog show that year's "holiday" instead.

A Breeder goes without sleep (but never without coffee!) through the hours spent planning a mating or keeping a watchful eye on a birth, and afterwards, on every sneeze, wriggle and whimper from the puppies.
A Breeder misses dinners because a litter is arriving or because the puppies need feeding at eight.
They think nothing of bodily fluids and give mouth-to-mouth to save a gasping newborn, literally breathing life into a tiny, helpless creature who may be the fulfilment of a lifetime of dreams.
A Breeder's lap is a wonderful place where generations of noble, proud champions once curled up.
A Breeder's hands are strong and steady, often worn, but always gentle and responsive to the nudge of a puppy's wet nose.
A Breeder's back and knees are often arthritic from bending over and sitting in whelping boxes, but still strong enough to take the next promising puppy into the ring on the road to a championship.
A Breeder's shoulders often sag under the harsh words of competitors, yet they are broad enough to bear the weight of a thousand defeats and disappointments.
A Breeder's arms are always ready to clean up any mess, carry an armful of puppies or lend a hand to a newcomer.

A Breeder's ears are a sight to behold: sometimes burning (from all the talk about them), sometimes oddly shaped (from being pressed against the phone so often). Yet they are always attuned to the whimper of a poorly puppy.
A Breeder's eyes are bleary from studying pedigrees and sometimes blind to their own dog's faults, yet always quick to spot those of the competition and always searching for the perfect dog.

A Breeder's mind may be hazy when it comes to faces, but it can recall pedigrees faster than a computer. It is so full that it sometimes blows a fuse: it catalogues thousands of sound bodies, correct angulations and perfect heads... and holds deep within the soul the faults and the ones who did not turn out as hoped.
A Breeder's heart is often broken, but it beats strongly with endless hope... and it is always in the right place!
